siem.description: SIEM configures the HTTPS batch sink for security information and event management systems, used by streams listing siem.

stdout.description: Stdout mirrors all streams to standard output (useful under journald and in containers).

syslog.description: Syslog configures the syslog sink used by streams listing it.

MFAPolicy.description: MFAPolicy is a second factor, shared by every protocol that can ask for one. It is one shape rather than one per protocol because a second factor that means different things on different ports is not a second factor: the same enrolment, the same replay rule and the same lockout have to hold everywhere, or the weakest door decides.

file.description: File is the enrolment file (xproxyctl mfa enrol writes the lines). Required. It must not be world readable.

issuer.description: Issuer is the name an authenticator application shows. Default "xproxy".

lockout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_failures.description: MaxFailures within Window locks a user out for Duration. Defaults 5, 5m and 15m. A six-digit code has a million values and a step lasts thirty seconds, so without a bound a fast client gets a real chance at every step.

max_users.description: MaxUsers bounds the table that remembers spent codes and recent failures. Default 10000.

prompt.description: Prompt is what the user is asked. Default "One-time code: ".

require_enrolment.description: RequireEnrolment refuses a user who has no enrolment. Default true: an optional second factor is one an attacker can decline by using an account that never enrolled.

skew.description: Skew is how many time steps either side of now are accepted. Default 1, which is the usual allowance for a clock that is a little off. Each step accepted is a step an observer could replay in, so this is not a knob to raise casually.

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

MQTTListener.description: MQTTListener is a protocol-aware MQTT proxy for 3.1.1 and 5.0. It reads every control packet, decides on the ones that carry a policy question — who is connecting, what they publish, what they subscribe to — and forwards the rest untouched. The reason it is not a layer 4 listener: an MQTT broker's authorisation is per topic, and a topic is a string inside a packet. Without reading the packets there is no place to say that a device may publish its own telemetry and nothing else, and every device that holds a broker credential holds the whole tree.

action.description: Action on a refused PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE: disconnect (the default) ends the session, drop refuses the one packet and acknowledges it so the session continues.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs.

allow_empty_client_id.description: AllowEmptyClientID accepts the empty client id, which 3.1.1 allows with a clean session and 5.0 answers with an assigned one. Default true; turning it off is what makes every session identifiable in the logs.

allow_retain.description: AllowRetain accepts PUBLISH with the retain flag. A retained message outlives the session that set it, so a device that can retain can leave something behind. Default true.

allow_wildcard_subscribe.description: AllowWildcardSubscribe accepts "+" and "#" in a subscription at all. Default true; with an allow list it rarely needs turning off, and without one it is the difference between a client reading its own topics and reading the estate's.

client_id_pattern.description: ClientIDPattern is an RE2 the client id must match, anchored as written. Empty accepts any.

connect_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

keep_alive_max.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_client_id.description: MaxClientID bounds the client id. Default 128.

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 10000.

max_packet_size.description: MaxPacketSize bounds one control packet including its header, and is what a 5.0 client is told in CONNACK. Default 1048576.

max_subscriptions.description: MaxSubscriptions bounds live subscriptions per session. Default 64.

max_topic_length.description: MaxTopicLength and MaxTopicLevels bound a topic or filter. Defaults 512 and 16.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header with the client address to the broker.

publish_allow.description: PublishAllow and PublishDeny are topic filters checked against the topic of every PUBLISH from the client, and against the will topic of its CONNECT. Deny wins. An empty allow list allows everything the deny list does not refuse.

require_auth.description: RequireAuth refuses a CONNECT without a username. The broker still verifies the password; this only stops an anonymous session reaching it. Default false.

subscribe_allow.description: SubscribeAllow and SubscribeDeny are topic filters checked against every filter a client subscribes to. A subscription is allowed only when an entry of the allow list covers everything it could deliver, and refused when it could reach anything denied — a filter is not a topic, and matching it as one would let "#" through an allow list of "sensors/+".

tls_mode.description: TLSMode is implicit (TLS from the first octet, as on 8883, and needs the listener's tls section) or none. Default implicit when tls is set.

upstream.description: Upstream is the broker pool. Required.

upstream_tls.description: UpstreamTLS verifies the broker when upstream_tls_mode is not none.

upstream_tls_mode.description: UpstreamTLSMode is none or implicit. Default none.

versions.description: Versions are the protocol versions accepted: "3.1.1", "5.0". Default both. A version the proxy does not parse cannot be checked, so anything else is refused at CONNECT.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs are always served (operators, health checkers).

allow_header.description: AllowHeader, "Name: value", exempts a request carrying it (a shared bypass token behind another gate).

enabled.description: Enabled is the state at start; the runtime toggle overrides it.

message.description: Message is the response body. Default a short text.

retry_after.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Management.description: Management configures the control plane listener used by xproxyctl.

history_dir.description: HistoryDir keeps every applied configuration as a file for xproxyctl history, diff and rollback. Empty disables history.

history_keep.description: HistoryKeep is how many entries are kept. Default 20.

socket.description: Socket is the path of the Unix domain socket. Empty disables management.

socket_mode.description: SocketMode is the octal permission mode of the socket, default 0660.

Masque.description: Masque configures UDP proxying (RFC 9298) and IP proxying (RFC 9484) over extended CONNECT. Both need HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, so the listener needs tls with h2 in its protocols.

ip.description: IP accepts connect-ip. It also needs ip_device, ip_assign and ip_routes: a userspace process cannot put an arbitrary IP packet on the wire without a tunnel device.

ip_assign.description: IPAssign are the prefixes a client is told to use as its source address; packets from anything else are dropped.

ip_device.description: IPDevice is an existing tun interface the operator created, addressed, routed and firewalled (Linux only).

ip_routes.description: IPRoutes are the ranges a client may send to; packets to anything else are dropped.

max_sessions.description: MaxSessions bounds concurrent MASQUE sessions. Default 1024.

udp.description: UDP accepts connect-udp. The destination policy applies to each association exactly as it does to a CONNECT tunnel.

Metrics.description: Metrics configures Prometheus exposition and sampled series (AMR-026). The management socket always serves /metrics; Listen adds a TCP endpoint for scrapers.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs restricts scrapers by source address. Empty allows any address that reaches the listener.

endpoint_series.description: EndpointSeries exposes five series per upstream endpoint. Default true; turn off above a few thousand endpoints (about 1 KiB per endpoint per scrape).

listen.description: Listen is an optional host:port serving only /metrics. Binding all interfaces requires TLS with a client CA.

otlp.description: OTLP pushes the same metrics to an OpenTelemetry collector.

per_route.description: PerRoute exposes request counters per route (one series per route and status class). Default true.

retention.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

sample_interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

tls.description: TLS makes the listener HTTPS; ClientCAFile requires client certificates.

MetricsTLS.description: MetricsTLS is the metrics listener certificate and optional client CA.

MirrorDiff.description: MirrorDiff configures the comparison of a shadow response with the live response. Status is always compared; headers are compared for the listed names; bodies are compared by length and digest up to MaxBodyBytes. The outcome is counted in xproxy_mirror_diff_total and a sampled share of the differing exchanges is logged.

headers.description: Headers are the response header names compared between the two responses. Empty compares no headers (status and body only).

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes bounds the bytes of each response digested for the body comparison. Default 64 KiB.

sample_percent.description: SamplePercent is the share of shadowed requests whose difference is logged (metrics count every one). Default 100.

Normalization.description: Normalization decides what the proxy does with encoding tricks in the request target before anything else looks at it. Routing already decodes and cleans the path; these checks refuse the forms that make two components disagree about what a request means, and optionally fold Unicode spellings for routing.

reject_ambiguous_framing.description: RejectAmbiguousFraming refuses HTTP/1 requests whose framing is ambiguous: both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length, several differing Content-Length values, or a transfer coding other than chunked. The Go parser already refuses most of these; the check closes the rest and counts them. Default true.

reject_backslashes.description: RejectBackslashes refuses a backslash anywhere in the decoded path. IIS, Apache on Windows and .NET read it as a separator while this proxy reads it as an ordinary character, so "/static\\..\\admin" is one opaque segment under /static here and "/admin" there: the route's access lists, filters, WAF profile and rate limits are all skipped for a resource the origin serves. Default true.

reject_control_chars.description: RejectControlChars refuses a decoded path or query containing a control character (below 0x20, or 0x7f), NUL included. Default true.

reject_dot_segments.description: RejectDotSegments refuses a "." or ".." segment in the decoded path (including the "..;" form servlet containers resolve). Routing resolves dot segments while the upstream receives the path as sent, so "/static/../admin" would be routed as "/admin" but reach the origin unchanged; browsers never send such paths. Default true.

reject_double_encoding.description: RejectDoubleEncoding refuses a path that still contains a percent escape after one decoding (%252e%252e). Default false.

reject_encoded_slashes.description: RejectEncodedSlashes refuses %2F and %5C in the raw path: the routing decoder turns them into separators that the upstream may treat as data. Default false.

reject_invalid_utf8.description: RejectInvalidUTF8 refuses a decoded path that is not valid UTF-8 (overlong and truncated sequences). Default true.

reject_path_params.description: RejectPathParams refuses a ";" in the decoded path. Tomcat, Jetty, JBoss and Spring strip a path parameter from every segment before mapping, so "/admin;x" or "/admin;jsessionid=..." misses this proxy's /admin route and its policy while the origin serves /admin. Default true.

unicode.description: Unicode is off, nfc or nfkc: the decoded path is normalised to that form for routing (the upstream receives the original), so composed and decomposed spellings, and with nfkc compatibility forms such as fullwidth letters, match the same route. Default off.

OCSPStapling.description: OCSPStapling configures the background OCSP fetcher of a listener.

refresh.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OTLP.description: OTLP is the OpenTelemetry push exporter: every interval the metric families are sent as OTLP/HTTP with JSON encoding to a collector (counters as cumulative monotonic sums, gauges, histograms as cumulative explicit bucket histograms).

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http endpoint.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the collector's CA. Default: system pool.

compress.description: Compress gzips the request body. Default true.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the collector's metrics URL, for example https://otel.example.com:4318/v1/metrics.

headers.description: Headers added to every request (for example Authorization).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

service_name.description: ServiceName is the service.name resource attribute. Default xproxy.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OTLPExport.description: OTLPExport is a collector endpoint for traces or logs.

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http endpoint.

batch.description: Batch is the largest number of items per push. Default 512.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the collector's CA. Default: system pool.

compress.description: Compress gzips the request body. Default true.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the collector URL (/v1/traces or /v1/logs).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

queue.description: Queue bounds items waiting for a push. Default 8192.

service_name.description: ServiceName is the service.name resource attribute. Default xproxy.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OriginSignature.description: OriginSignature is the bypass protection an origin verifies: an HMAC over method, host, path, query, time, client address, request id and the listed extra headers, carried in one header.

body_digest.description: BodyDigest makes the signature cover the request body of methods that carry one, as a SHA-256 the proxy also sends in Content-Digest. Default false. Without it a signature proves that a request passed through the proxy, not what it carried: anything that can reach the origin can replay a captured header set with a body of its own while the timestamp is inside the TTL. It costs buffering the body, and a bodied request larger than 8 MiB is refused rather than forwarded with a signature that stops at the headers.

header.description: Header carries the signature. Default X-Xproxy-Signature.

include.description: Include lists extra request headers covered by the signature.

secret_file.description: SecretFile is the keyring shared with the origin (created when missing; rotate with xproxyctl rotate-secret, the previous key stays valid for verification).

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OutlierEjection.description: OutlierEjection configures passive health checking: consecutive failures and, when latency_threshold or latency_factor is set, an endpoint whose smoothed time to first byte is slow.

base_ejection_time.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

latency_factor.description: LatencyFactor ejects an endpoint whose smoothed latency exceeds the pool's smoothed latency times this factor (at least 1.5), when the pool has two or more endpoints. 0 disables.

latency_min_samples.description: LatencyMinSamples is how many responses an endpoint must have answered since it last became available before its latency is judged. Default 20.

latency_threshold.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression matched anywhere in the body.

content_types.description: ContentTypes narrows the inspection to these media types (type/* allowed). Empty inspects every body.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes bounds the body inspected. Default 64 KiB.

over_limit.description: OverLimit decides a body larger than MaxBytes, or one the filter could not read: "match" (default) treats it as matching the patch, "skip" lets it through unmatched. A virtual patch is the emergency control that holds a known vulnerability while the application is fixed, and every sibling control here refuses an oversize body rather than passing it. With "skip", 64 KiB of padding carries the same payload straight to the origin.

PatchMatch.description: PatchMatch is one condition on a named parameter, header or cookie.

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression matched anywhere in a value; empty means presence suffices.

QueryParamPolicy.description: QueryParamPolicy describes one allowed query parameter.

type.description: Type is string (default), int, number, bool, uuid or enum (with Values).

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression every value must match in full.

required.description: Required refuses requests without the parameter.

max_length.description: MaxLength bounds each value; 0 means no bound.

max_repeat.description: MaxRepeat bounds how many times the parameter may appear. Default 1.

values.description: Values are the allowed values for type enum.

RDPChannelPolicy.description: RDPChannelPolicy decides which static virtual channels a session has. A channel that is not allowed is taken out of the list the desktop is asked for, so the desktop never learns it was wanted.

allow.description: Allow names the channels a client may have. The default is none: a session that can see the desktop and nothing else.

RDPDevicePolicy.description: RDPDevicePolicy decides which kinds of redirected device a session has, among the ones the rdpdr channel carries: drive, printer, serial, parallel, smartcard. It applies only where rdpdr is an allowed channel, since without the channel there is nothing to announce a device on.

allow.description: Allow names the device kinds a client may redirect. The default is none, so allowing the rdpdr channel without naming a device kind gives a session no redirection at all.

RDPListener.description: RDPListener is a Remote Desktop gateway: the proxy terminates the connection sequence on both legs, which is what lets it decide the security protocol, rewrite the virtual channel list, check a second factor against the credential in flight, substitute the credential that opens the desktop, and record what the session showed. The channel list is the important one. Every redirection RDP has -- drives, printers, serial and parallel ports, smart cards, the clipboard, audio -- rides a virtual channel, and nothing can be used that was not both announced and granted. A gateway that rewrites the list decides what a session is able to do, before it does it.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs.

channels.description: Channels is the static virtual channel policy.

devices.description: Devices is the redirected device policy, which is what decides whether a session can move a file or reach a port.

handshake_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 200.

mfa.description: MFA asks for a one-time code, carried with the password since RDP has nowhere to ask a question.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header to the desktop.

recording.description: Recording writes the session stream to a file.

security.description: Security is what a client may use, by name: tls or rdp. Default tls. nla is not offered to clients and cannot be: checking it would need every person's password, which is the one thing a gateway should not hold. See docs/CONFIG.md.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of desktops. Required.

upstream_security.description: UpstreamSecurity is what this proxy uses towards the desktop, by name: tls, nla or rdp. Default tls.

upstream_tls.description: UpstreamTLS pins the CA and name for the desktop's leg.

upstream_user.description: UpstreamUser and UpstreamPasswordFile are the credential this proxy opens the desktop with, where an operator would rather the person's own never reached it. Without them the person's credential is forwarded as it arrived.

RateLimit.description: RateLimit is a named rate limit policy referenced by routes: a token bucket (rate and burst) or a sliding window (limit per window).

action.description: Action is reject (429) or tarpit. Default reject.

algorithm.description: Algorithm is token_bucket (default; rate and burst) or sliding_window (limit and window).

distributed.description: Distributed selects the cluster semantics: approximate (default; each node refills at the rate minus its peers' reported consumption) or exact (one node owns each key, chosen by rendezvous hashing over the connected members, and decides for the others; a node that cannot reach the owner within cluster.exact_timeout decides locally). Needs the cluster section.

key.description: Key selects the bucket identity: client_ip, client_net, route, country, endpoint, ja4, header:<name>, cookie:<name> or jwt:<claim>. Keys that a request may lack fall back to the client address.

limit.description: Limit is the number of requests allowed per Window (sliding_window).

net_v4.description: NetV4 and NetV6 are the prefix lengths for key client_net. Default 24 and 48.

tarpit_delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Redaction.description: Redaction rules. Presence enables them; Enabled false switches them off without removing the configuration.

claims.description: Claims is keep, hash or drop and applies to jwt_* attributes and client_cn. Default hash.

client_ip.description: ClientIP is keep, truncate (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) or hash (keyed HMAC-SHA256, stable per installation). Default truncate.

drop_fields.description: DropFields lists further attribute names removed from log lines.

hash_secret_file.description: HashSecretFile holds the key for hash mode; created on first use.

referer.description: Referer is keep, origin (scheme and host only) or drop. Default origin.

streams.description: Streams the rules apply to. Default [access, security, error]; the audit stream keeps full detail unless listed.

user_agent.description: UserAgent is keep or drop. Default keep.

Redirect.description: Redirect is a static redirect action. To may use the request variables (${path}, ${raw_query}, ${host}, ${1}...) to build the target.

Respond.description: Respond is a static response action.

RetryBudget.description: RetryBudget limits the rate of retries relative to live requests. A retry (or a hedged copy) is only sent while the number of retries in flight to the pool stays below Percent of the requests in flight, with MinConcurrency always allowed so a low-traffic pool can still retry.

min_concurrency.description: MinConcurrency is the number of concurrent retries always allowed regardless of Percent, so a pool with little live traffic can still retry. Default 3; 1 to 10000.

percent.description: Percent caps retries in flight at this share of requests in flight. Default 20; 1 to 1000.

RewriteRegex.description: RewriteRegex is a regular expression path rewrite. Replace may use ${1} to ${9} and ${name} for the pattern's groups, and the request variables of header templates (docs/CONFIG.md, "Variables").

Route.description: Route maps a request to an upstream and attaches policies.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs / DenyCIDRs implement simple IP access control. Deny is evaluated first. Empty allow means allow all.

cache.description: Cache stores responses of this route (needs the cache section).

challenge.description: Challenge gates unverified clients with the browser challenge.

client_cert_headers.description: ClientCertHeaders states the client's TLS certificate to the backend: none (the default), rfc9440 (Client-Cert and Client-Cert-Chain, RFC 9440) or xfcc (Envoy's X-Forwarded-Client-Cert). Whatever this says, a client's own copy of any of those headers is removed from every request that did not arrive from a peer inside trusted_proxies: the backend cannot tell the proxy's header from the client's, so a client that can send one chooses its own identity.

compress.description: Compress overrides the compression section for this route: false turns it off, true requires the section.

compress_authenticated.description: CompressAuthenticated overrides compression.compress_authenticated for this route.

cors.description: CORS answers cross-origin requests for this route: it short-circuits preflight OPTIONS and adds the response headers to actual requests.

deceive.description: Deceive answers a client this route no longer trusts with a plausible response instead of the origin's.

doh.description: DoH answers DNS over HTTPS on this route through a dns listener.

error_pages.description: ErrorPages overrides the server's error pages for this route.

filters.description: Filters names entries of the top-level filters list, run in the listed order within their stage.

geo.description: Geo allows or denies by client country (needs the geoip section).

grpc.description: GRPC restricts the route to gRPC requests, optionally to listed services or methods.

headers.description: Headers and Cookies are conditions on the request: every listed match must hold. Entries with conditions rank above entries without at the same path length (more conditions first).

honeypot.description: Honeypot serves a decoy and marks the client instead of proxying.

host_header.description: HostHeader overrides the Host header sent upstream. Default keeps the client Host.

hosts.description: Hosts are exact host names or wildcard patterns ("*.example.com"). Empty matches any host.

icap.description: ICAP hands requests and/or responses to a scanning service.

jwt.description: JWT requires or accepts a validated token from a provider.

maintenance.description: Maintenance overrides the global maintenance gate for this route: false always serves it (health, status), true always holds it.

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes overrides the global body limit for this route (may only lower it unless allow_raise is set).

mirror.description: Mirror copies requests of this route to a second upstream.

path_regex.description: PathRegex lists RE2 patterns that must match the whole cleaned path (anchored at both ends by the proxy). A regex entry ranks by the length of its literal prefix; at equal length it beats a prefix entry. With PathRegex set, Paths has no default.

paths.description: Paths are prefixes. "/" matches everything. Longest prefix wins.

policy.description: Policy is the route's positive security model: what a request may look like; everything else is refused before any other processing.

priority.description: Priority breaks ties between routes with identical specificity. Higher wins. Default 0.

priority_class.description: PriorityClass is low, normal, high or critical (never shed). Default normal.

redirect.description: Redirect answers with a redirect instead of proxying.

respond.description: Respond answers with a static status instead of proxying.

rewrite_regex.description: RewriteRegex rewrites the outbound path with a regular expression and capture groups; exclusive with rewrite_path, applied after strip_prefix. A path that does not match is sent unchanged.

static.description: Static serves files from a directory instead of proxying.

tenant.description: Tenant is a free label that groups routes for quota reporting (GET /v1/quotas, xproxyctl quotas) and the per route metrics.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

waf.description: WAF overrides the global WAF mode and profile for this route.

websocket.description: WebSocket allows Upgrade: websocket to be forwarded. Default false.

websocket_guard.description: WebSocketGuard inspects the frames of an upgraded connection. Without it an upgrade is an opaque tunnel.

webtransport.description: WebTransport relays WebTransport sessions (extended CONNECT over HTTP/3 on a listener with h3) to the upstream, which must speak HTTP/3 (h3: true): bidirectional and unidirectional streams and datagrams in both directions. Default false.

when.description: When is a condition in the expression language (docs/CONFIG.md, "Expressions") that must hold in addition to the matches above; it counts as one condition for specificity.

RouteCORS.description: RouteCORS is a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policy for a route. It is independent of the gRPC-web preflight handling (grpc.web_origins).

allow_credentials.description: AllowCredentials sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and echoes the specific origin (never "*").

allow_headers.description: AllowHeaders are the request headers a preflight may allow; "*" reflects the requested headers. Default: reflect the request's Access-Control-Request-Headers.

allow_methods.description: AllowMethods default to GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

allow_origins.description: AllowOrigins are the permitted Origin values: exact ("https://a.example"), a single "*" (any origin; incompatible with allow_credentials), or a wildcard host pattern ("https://*.example.com"). Required.

max_age.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RouteCache.description: RouteCache is a route's caching policy.

cookies.description: Cookies allows caching requests that carry a Cookie header. Default false: such requests bypass the cache.

headers.description: Headers are request headers whose values join the key (for example Accept-Encoding when the upstream does not send Vary).

ignore_cache_control.description: IgnoreCacheControl stores responses regardless of Cache-Control and applies ttl. Default false.

query.description: Query is "all" (default), "none" (ignore the query string in the key) or "listed" (only the names in query_params, sorted).

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RouteChallenge.description: RouteChallenge selects when a route challenges unverified clients.

level.description: Level is the load level that activates load mode. Default 0.5.

mode.description: Mode is off, always or load. In load mode clients are challenged only while the shedding load level is at or above Level.

RouteDoH.description: RouteDoH is the DNS over HTTPS action (RFC 8484): GET with a base64url dns parameter or POST with an application/dns-message body, answered by the named kind: dns listener's policy and cache.

RouteGRPC.description: RouteGRPC matches gRPC requests (content type application/grpc) by the service and method in the path (/package.Service/Method). Empty lists match every gRPC request. Denials and proxy errors on such a route are answered as gRPC statuses.

services.description: Services are fully qualified service names.

web.description: Web accepts gRPC-web requests from browsers (application/grpc-web and grpc-web-text, over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2) and translates them to gRPC for the upstream: the response trailers become a trailer frame in the body and the text variant is base64 encoded. Default false.

web_origins.description: WebOrigins answers CORS preflights of gRPC-web clients from these origins (exact, or "*") and adds the allow and expose headers to responses. Empty handles no CORS.

RouteGeo.description: RouteGeo is a country policy. Deny is evaluated first; a non-empty Allow admits only the listed countries. Unknown says what happens to an address the database does not know: allow (default) or deny.

RouteICAP.description: RouteICAP attaches a service to a route.

request.description: Request sends requests (REQMOD); Response sends responses (RESPMOD). Request defaults to true, Response to false.

RouteJWT.description: RouteJWT attaches a provider to a route.

required.description: Required rejects requests without a token with 401. Default true. When false, a missing token passes and an invalid one is rejected.

RouteMirror.description: RouteMirror sends a copy of each request (sampled by percent) to another upstream in the background. The copy carries the same path rules, host and header operations as the live request plus X-Xproxy-Mirror: 1; its response is discarded and never affects the client. Bodies are buffered up to max_body_bytes; larger requests are proxied but not mirrored.

diff.description: Diff compares the shadow response with the live one and reports the differences, turning the mirror into traffic shadowing for validating a new backend against the current one. Off when unset.

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes bounds the buffered body. Default 1 MiB.

max_in_flight.description: MaxInFlight bounds copies in flight for this route; beyond it copies are dropped and counted. Default 64.

methods.description: Methods restricts copies to these methods. Empty copies every method except upgrades.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RoutePolicy.description: RoutePolicy is a positive security model for a route: allowed methods, media types and query parameters, and bounds on the URI, headers and query. A request outside the policy is refused (405, 415, 400, 414 or 431) with reason policy before rate limits, filters and the WAF run, and the refusal feeds ban triggers under policy.

content_types.description: ContentTypes allowed for requests with a body: media types or type/* patterns; others get 415. Empty allows any.

max_headers.description: MaxHeaders bounds the number of header fields; MaxHeaderBytes the sum of their names and values. 0 means no bound (the server limit still applies).

max_query_bytes.description: MaxQueryBytes bounds the raw query string; MaxQueryParams the number of parameters (repeats counted). 0 means no bound.

max_uri_length.description: MaxURILength lowers server.limits.max_uri_length for the route.

methods.description: Methods allowed; others get 405 with an Allow header. Unlike routes[].methods, which selects the route, this refuses. Empty allows any method.

query.description: Query describes the parameters; with DenyUnknown, parameters not listed are refused.

require_content_type.description: RequireContentType refuses a body without a Content-Type header.

RouteStatic.description: RouteStatic serves files from a directory. Paths are resolved inside Root with os.Root, so neither ".." nor a symbolic link can leave it.

cache_control.description: CacheControl is sent with every file. Default none.

dot_files.description: DotFiles serves names starting with a dot. Default false.

fallback.description: Fallback is a path inside Root served when the requested file does not exist (single page applications: /index.html). Default none.

index.description: Index is the file served for a directory. Default index.html; empty string disables ("" in YAML).

listing.description: Listing renders a directory without an index. Default false.

max_file_bytes.description: MaxFileBytes refuses larger files with 404. Default 0 (no bound).

root.description: Root is the absolute directory served.

RouteTimeouts.description: RouteTimeouts are a route's named timeouts. Connect and the response header timeout are configured per upstream (upstreams[].timeouts), since the connection pool is shared; these bound the exchange as a whole and the gaps between response bytes.

idle.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

total.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RouteWAF.description: RouteWAF selects the WAF profile and mode for a route.

block_cidrs.description: BlockCIDRs always get block mode whatever the share: the canary clients (internal testers, a pilot customer). Only with mode block.

block_percent.description: BlockPercent rolls block mode out gradually: this share of the clients (a stable function of the client address) gets block mode, the rest detect mode. Default 100. Only with mode block.

mode.description: Mode is off, detect or block.

SFTPPolicy.description: SFTPPolicy inspects the SFTP protocol inside an sftp subsystem channel. Refused requests are answered with a permission-denied status, so the session continues and the client is told which operation was refused rather than losing its connection.

allow_extensions.description: AllowExtensions are the file extensions a name may carry, without the dot and compared without case. Empty allows every extension the deny list does not refuse. It is checked on open, and on both names of a rename or a symlink, which are the requests that decide what a file is called.

allow_paths.description: AllowPaths are the paths a request may name: a glob where "*" does not cross a slash, or a prefix ending in "/" or "/**" for a whole tree. Empty allows every path the deny list does not refuse. A pattern may carry {user} or {principal}, which are the login the session authenticated as and the principals entry that covers it. They are substituted once per session, which is what lets one listener say "your own directory and no other" instead of one list naming everybody's.

deny_extensions.description: DenyExtensions are refused whatever the allow list says. A name is read for every extension it carries, so "invoice.pdf.exe" is an exe whatever the list allows.

deny_operations.description: DenyOperations refuses operations by name (open, read, write, remove, rename, symlink, setstat, ...), on top of read_only.

deny_paths.description: DenyPaths are refused whatever the allow list says. They take the same {user} and {principal} substitutions.

icap.description: ICAP hands written files to a scanning service. SFTP has no whole-file transfer: a file is a handle, a run of writes at offsets, and a close. So the proxy holds the writes rather than forwarding them, answers the client itself, scans what the file turned out to be when the handle is closed, and only then replays the writes to the server. A file the scanner refuses never reaches it, at the cost of holding it in memory until the close -- bounded by the service's max_body, past which body_limit_action decides.

max_file_bytes.description: MaxFileBytes bounds what one open file may be written. 0 is no bound. It is counted per handle, from the highest offset a write reaches, so a client cannot walk past it by writing out of order.

max_open_files.description: MaxOpenFiles bounds the handles one session may have open at once, which is what the per file state costs. Default 256.

max_packet_size.description: MaxPacketSize bounds one SFTP packet. Default 262144, a little over the 32 KiB read and write sizes clients use.

read_only.description: ReadOnly refuses every request that changes the server: write, setstat, remove, mkdir, rmdir, rename, symlink, an open with any writing flag, and the extensions whose meaning the proxy does not know.

yara.description: YARA scans what is written, per file rather than per stream: a rule about a file's first bytes is a rule about a file, and two uploads interleaved on one channel are two files. A match refuses that write; directions is not read here, because only what the client writes is a file this proxy is choosing to accept.

SIEM.description: SIEM is an HTTP collector of a SIEM: Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Elastic or OpenSearch ingest, Microsoft Sentinel, or any endpoint that accepts newline delimited JSON, CEF or LEEF.

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http endpoint.

auth_file.description: AuthFile holds the Authorization header value ("Splunk <token>", "Bearer <token>", "ApiKey <key>"), kept out of the configuration.

batch.description: Batch is the largest number of records per push. Default 512.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the collector's CA; CertFile and KeyFile present a client certificate.

compress.description: Compress gzips the request body. Default true.

format.description: Format is json (newline delimited JSON lines), hec (the Splunk HTTP Event Collector envelope), cef or leef. Default json.

hostname.description: Hostname is the device host name reported (dvchost, identHostName, the HEC host). Default the OS host name.

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

queue.description: Queue bounds records waiting for a push. Default 8192.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

vendor.description: Vendor and Product fill the CEF and LEEF header fields. Defaults Sysctl and Xproxy.

SMTPListener.description: SMTPListener is a protocol-aware SMTP proxy: it speaks the session to the client, speaks a second one to the upstream, and decides for itself where each command and each message ends. That is the point of it. A layer 4 splice would carry the same bytes, but the client and the mail server would each parse them on their own, and every SMTP smuggling bug there has ever been lives in the gap between two such parses. It terminates STARTTLS (RFC 3207) for the client and may start its own to the upstream, so the hop the proxy makes is never the plaintext one by accident.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs. Empty allows all, which is right for inbound mail and wrong for submission.

banner.description: Banner replaces the upstream greeting. The proxy's own name belongs here; leaving the upstream's banner in place tells every prober which mail server is behind this address.

bare_newlines.description: BareNewlines is reject (the default) or convert. A line ended by LF alone is forbidden by RFC 5321 section 2.3.8 and is how a message ends in one place for the proxy and another for the next hop; convert repairs it to CRLF instead of refusing the session, which is safe because the proxy re-emits every line itself.

commands.description: Commands is the verbs a client may send. Everything else is refused with 502 and counts towards max_errors. Default: EHLO, HELO, MAIL, RCPT, DATA, RSET, NOOP, QUIT, AUTH, STARTTLS.

hide_capabilities.description: HideCapabilities are EHLO keywords stripped from the upstream's answer, on top of the ones the proxy always removes (STARTTLS, which it answers itself, and CHUNKING, whose BDAT has no dot terminator to agree on). Default: none.

hostname.description: Hostname is the name the proxy gives as its own in a synthesised greeting and in its EHLO to the upstream. Default the banner's first word, else the system hostname.

max_command_line.description: MaxCommandLine bounds a command line including CRLF. Default 512, the limit in RFC 5321 section 4.5.3.1.1.

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 1000.

max_errors.description: MaxErrors closes the session after this many refused commands, which is what stops a prober walking the command space. Default 10.

max_message_size.description: MaxMessageSize bounds one message in octets and is advertised as the SIZE capability. 0 keeps the upstream's own limit. Default 0.

max_messages.description: MaxMessages bounds messages per connection. Default 100.

max_recipients.description: MaxRecipients bounds RCPT commands per message. Default 100.

max_text_line.description: MaxTextLine bounds a message line including CRLF. Default 1000.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header to the upstream so it logs the client address rather than the proxy's.

read_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

require_auth.description: RequireAuth refuses MAIL until the session has authenticated, which keeps a submission listener from relaying for anyone who can reach it. Default false: a listener taking inbound mail for its own domains has no authentication to require.

require_tls.description: RequireTLS refuses AUTH, MAIL and VRFY until the session is encrypted. On a submission listener this is the difference between offering TLS and requiring it. Default true when TLSMode is starttls or implicit.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

tls_mode.description: TLSMode is how the client reaches this listener: starttls (plain on 25 or 587, upgraded by the STARTTLS command), implicit (TLS from the first octet, as on 465) or none. starttls and implicit need the listener's tls section. Default starttls when tls is set and none otherwise.

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool to relay to. Required.

upstream_tls.description: UpstreamTLS verifies the upstream when upstream_tls_mode is not none.

upstream_tls_mode.description: UpstreamTLSMode is how the proxy reaches the upstream: none, starttls or implicit. Default none, which is right when the hop is inside a trusted network and wrong everywhere else.

xclient.description: XClientName sends the client address to the upstream with the XCLIENT command (a Postfix extension) after EHLO, when the upstream advertises it.

SSHListener.description: SSHListener is an SSH bastion: the proxy is an SSH server to the client and an SSH client to the target, with its own host key, its own authentication and its own credential onwards. The two connections are the point. A jump host that forwards the stream cannot see which channel is a shell and which is a port forward, so the only policy it can hold is "may connect". Here every channel and every request inside the session is a decision: a service account can be given sftp to one directory and nothing else, and a port forward to a database is a rule rather than an assumption. It also means the target never sees the client's key. The client authenticates to the proxy; the proxy authenticates to the target with a credential the client never holds, so a key that leaves the estate is not a key that opens a server in it.

allow_channels.description: AllowChannels are the channel types a client may open: session, direct-tcpip (local port forwarding), direct-streamlocal (unix socket forwarding). Default [session].

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs.

allow_commands.description: AllowCommands are RE2 patterns an exec command must match, anchored as written. Empty allows any command when exec is in allow_requests.

allow_env.description: AllowEnv are the environment variables a client may set, as names or name prefixes ending in "*". Default TERM, LANG and LC_*. The loader and interpreter variables (LD_*, BASH_ENV, PERL5OPT, PYTHONPATH and their kin) are refused whatever this says: passing one to a target is handing it code to run before the command the policy approved.

allow_file_transfer_commands.description: AllowFileTransferCommands accepts exec commands that are file transfer helpers: scp, rsync --server, sftp-server. Default false when sftp is configured and true when it is not. The default is the point. An estate that carefully sets a read-only sftp policy and then allows exec has left "scp -t" wide open, because scp moves files without touching the sftp subsystem at all.

allow_requests.description: AllowRequests are the session requests a client may send: pty-req, env, shell, exec, subsystem, window-change, signal, x11-req, auth-agent-req. Default everything but x11-req and auth-agent-req, which each hand the target a channel back into the client.

allow_shell_syntax.description: AllowShellSyntax lets an exec command carry shell metacharacters. Default false. allow_commands is a list of regular expressions over the command line, and a regular expression is a weak thing to hold a shell to: "^journalctl .*$" matches "journalctl -u x; rm -rf /" exactly as happily as it matches what it was written for. So the command line is read as a shell would split it first, and one carrying an operator -- a semicolon, a pipe, an ampersand, a redirection, a backquote, a $( -- is refused before any pattern is tried. A listener that genuinely needs shell syntax sets this and writes its patterns accordingly.

allow_subsystems.description: AllowSubsystems are the subsystems a client may start. Default [sftp].

authorized_keys.description: AuthorizedKeys is an OpenSSH authorized_keys file of the public keys that may connect. Options in the file are ignored; the policy lives here.

banner.description: Banner is sent before authentication. A legal notice belongs here; a version string does not.

forward.description: Forward are the destinations direct-tcpip channels may reach: "host:port", "*.suffix:port", "10.0.0.0/8:port", with "*" for any port. Empty refuses every forward even when the channel type is allowed, because a forward with no destination policy is a tunnel to anywhere the target can reach.

handshake_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

host_keys.description: HostKeys are the proxy's own host key files, in OpenSSH or PEM form. At least one is required. Clients pin these, so replacing them is a fleet-wide known_hosts change: add the new key alongside the old one and remove the old one later.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_auth_tries.description: MaxAuthTries bounds authentication attempts per connection. Default 3.

max_certificate_lifetime.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_channels.description: MaxChannels bounds open channels per connection. Default 16.

max_forwards.description: MaxForwards bounds the port forwards one session may hold open at once. Default 8. A session that may forward at all can otherwise open one per file descriptor the proxy has.

max_sessions.description: MaxSessions bounds connections on this listener. Default 1000.

max_sessions_per_principal.description: MaxSessionsPerPrincipal bounds the sessions one principal may hold at once, which max_sessions cannot: a listener bounded at five hundred is five hundred for one key as much as for the fleet. Default 0, no bound.

mfa.description: MFA requires a second factor after the key or the password: the client is told authentication partially succeeded and must then answer a keyboard-interactive prompt with a one-time code.

principals.description: Principals give one key or one certificate principal its own policy. Without them the listener's policy is the same for everyone who gets past authentication, which is the policy a jump host can hold and not much more. The first entry that matches decides. When any are configured, a client matching none of them is refused: the list is the policy, so falling back to the listener's would be the opposite of what it says. An entry naming neither a fingerprint nor a certificate principal is the default, and must be last.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header with the client address to the target before the SSH banner.

recording.description: Recording writes what a session showed, and optionally what was typed into it, to a file per channel.

rekey_bytes.description: RekeyBytes is how many bytes pass before the transport agrees a fresh key. Default 0, which leaves the crypto library's own threshold (1 GiB, or 1 << 32 for a 64 bit block cipher).

remote_forward.description: RemoteForward accepts tcpip-forward, which asks the target to listen on the client's behalf. Default false: it turns a session into an inbound path.

revoked_keys.description: RevokedKeys is a file of public keys, in authorized_keys format, that are refused whatever else says otherwise: the key itself, a certificate whose key it is, and a certificate signed by it. It is the one list that overrides the CA, which is what makes a certificate revocable before it expires.

server_version.description: ServerVersion is the identification string, which must begin with "SSH-2.0-". Default "SSH-2.0-xproxy".

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

sftp.description: SFTP inspects the sftp subsystem's own protocol; without it the proxy can say only that a session may use sftp, which is the difference between reading a file and deleting a tree.

trusted_user_ca_keys.description: TrustedUserCAKeys is a file of CA public keys, in authorized_keys form. A client may then authenticate with a certificate signed by one of them instead of appearing in authorized_keys, and the certificate's principals decide which entry of principals applies to it. A certificate that has expired, is not yet valid, or does not list the name the client is connecting as is refused.

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of target hosts. Required.

upstream_insecure_host_key.description: UpstreamInsecureHostKey accepts any host key from the target. Refused unless allow_insecure is also set, and logged at start: it is the one setting here that turns the bastion into a machine in the middle with nothing to notice it.

upstream_key_file.description: UpstreamKeyFile is the private key the proxy authenticates to the target with. Required.

upstream_known_hosts.description: UpstreamKnownHosts verifies the target's host key against an OpenSSH known_hosts file. Required unless upstream_insecure_host_key is set.

upstream_user.description: UpstreamUser is the account on the target. Empty uses the name the client authenticated as.

users_file.description: UsersFile is a users file (as in forward.auth) for password authentication. Public keys are the better answer; a bastion with only passwords is one credential away from open.

SSHPolicy.description: SSHPolicy is the part of an ssh listener's policy a principal can have its own copy of. Every field is optional: unset means the listener's value.

deny.description: Deny refuses this principal outright, which is how a key stays in authorized_keys while the person it belongs to is off.

recording.description: Recording replaces the listener's, which is how one entry is recorded and another is not. A principal that should not be recorded where the listener is sets enabled: false.

SSHPrincipal.description: SSHPrincipal gives one key, or one certificate principal, its own policy on an ssh listener.

cert_principals.description: CertPrincipals are the principals of a certificate this entry covers; they need trusted_user_ca_keys.

fingerprints.description: Fingerprints are SHA256 fingerprints of the keys this entry covers, in the form ssh-keygen prints: "SHA256:" and the base64 of the digest.

name.description: Name appears in the access log and the security events, so a refusal names a person rather than a fingerprint.

policy.description: Policy is what this principal may do. Anything it leaves unset falls back to the listener's own setting, so an entry that only changes the target account says only that.

users.description: Users restricts the entry to these login names. Empty matches any name the key authenticated as.

Sandbox.description: Sandbox configures the in-process hardening (docs/HARDENING.md). Every mechanism is applied after the listeners, log files, state files and the management socket are open, so the rules describe what the process still needs afterwards: the directories of every configured file for reading, the log, state and history directories for writing. A reload that names a file outside those directories is refused with a message to restart, because Landlock rules cannot be widened once applied.

capabilities.description: Capabilities clears the bounding, ambient, permitted, effective and inheritable sets (Linux). Default true.

debuggable.description: Debuggable keeps the process attachable by a debugger and able to dump core. Default false: the process is made non dumpable and the core size limit is set to zero, so memory holding keys and request data cannot be read by another process of the same user or written to disk.

enabled.description: Enabled applies the sandbox. Default true.

landlock.description: Landlock restricts file system access to the derived directories (Linux 5.13 or newer) and, on ABI 4 or newer, refuses new TCP binds.

no_new_privs.description: NoNewPrivs sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS so that no later exec (there is none) could regain privileges; Landlock and unprivileged seccomp require it. Default true.

seccomp.description: Seccomp installs a system call deny list: process tracing, module loading, mounts, namespaces, keyrings, BPF, io_uring, identity changes, exec and the kernel administration calls return EPERM (Linux).

strict.description: Strict refuses to start when a mechanism the platform should offer is unavailable (old kernel, container without the syscall) instead of logging and continuing. Default false.

drop.description: Drop clears every capability set. Default true.

bind.description: Bind refuses TCP binds after start (Landlock ABI 4, Linux 6.7 or newer). Listeners are bound before the sandbox; a reload that adds a listener requires a restart in any case. Default true.

enabled.description: Enabled applies Landlock when the kernel offers it. Default true.

read_paths.description: ReadPaths are extra files or directories the process may read (a filter that opens files of its own, a certificate directory that reloads will add files to).

write_paths.description: WritePaths are extra directories the process may write.

SandboxSeccomp.description: SandboxSeccomp tunes the system call filter.

enabled.description: Enabled installs the filter. Default true.

SecurityTxt.description: SecurityTxt is one virtual security.txt document (RFC 9116) and the requests it answers. The proxy serves it at /.well-known/security.txt and at the legacy /security.txt, before routing, so a host with no route of its own still has one — which is the parked name a finder tries first. Entries are tried in order and the first whose selectors all match answers, so an entry with no selectors placed last is the fallback for every other host. A request that matches no entry is routed as usual, so an origin serving its own file keeps doing so.

acknowledgments.description: Acknowledgments points at a page thanking finders.

body.description: Body is the document verbatim, for a signed file kept elsewhere. Exclusive with the fields above.

body_file.description: BodyFile is read at load and on every reload, at most 64 KiB. Use it for a clear-signed document, which cannot be assembled from fields without breaking the signature.

cache_for.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

canonical.description: Canonical is where this document is expected to be found; it is what makes a copy found elsewhere recognisable as a copy.

client_cidrs.description: ClientCIDRs restrict the entry to clients inside these networks, so an internal document can differ from the public one.

comment.description: Comment is placed at the top of the document, each line prefixed with "# ".

contact.description: Contact is one or more ways to report, most preferred first (mailto:, tel: or https:). Required unless body or body_file is set.

csaf.description: CSAF points at a provider-metadata.json (RFC 9116 section 2.5.4).

encryption.description: Encryption points at a key a finder should encrypt to.

expires.description: Expires is an RFC 3339 instant after which the document should not be used. Exclusive with valid_for.

extra.description: Extra carries fields this build does not know by name, rendered after the known ones in name order.

hiring.description: Hiring points at security job openings.

host_cidrs.description: HostCIDRs match a request whose Host is an address literal rather than a name, against these networks: the parked addresses, a range a provider assigned, or "0.0.0.0/0" and "::/0" for every literal there is. This is the selector for the host a scanner reaches by address because no name points at it, which is exactly where a finder has nothing else to go on. A Host that is a name is never matched by it, whatever that name resolves to: the proxy does not resolve the Host header.

host_regex.description: HostRegex additionally matches the host against an RE2 expression, for a naming scheme a wildcard cannot express.

hosts.description: Hosts are exact names or wildcard patterns ("*.example.com", which matches a label or more and not the bare name). Empty matches every host.

listeners.description: Listeners restrict the entry to these listener names.

name.description: Name identifies the entry in the status view and the access log.

policy.description: Policy points at the disclosure policy.

preferred_languages.description: PreferredLanguages are BCP 47 tags, rendered as one field.

valid_for.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Server.description: Server holds listener and global limit settings for the data plane.

error_pages.description: ErrorPages replaces the proxy's plain status bodies for every route (routes may override).

normalization.description: Normalization checks and canonicalises the request target before routing and analysis.

server_header.description: ServerHeader is the value sent in the Server response header. Empty removes the header entirely (the default) to avoid fingerprinting.

session_tickets.description: SessionTickets derives the TLS session ticket keys of every TLS listener from a master secret file and the time, so nodes sharing the file resume each other's sessions and keys rotate on schedule without a restart. Without the section each process uses random keys that rotate every 24 hours and are never shared.

shutdown_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

zone.description: Zone names the failure domain this node is in -- an availability zone, a rack, a site. It is what an upstream's locality policy compares an endpoint's zone against, so a node prefers the endpoints beside it. Empty means the node does not know where it is, and a locality policy then prefers nothing.

SessionRecording.description: SessionRecording records an interactive session to a file that can be replayed. A bastion's access log says a session happened; it cannot say what was done in it, because what was done is a stream of control sequences inside the channel. This writes that stream, in the asciicast v2 format, so the question "what did they actually run" has an answer that is watched rather than reconstructed. The files hold everything the session showed, which on an administrative session is a list of everything worth having: keys printed, configuration read, tokens echoed. They are treated the way the capture files are — the proxy user's alone, in a directory the operator names — and they are a reason to keep that directory as carefully as the credentials it will end up holding.

commands.description: Commands records exec sessions too, not only the ones with a terminal. Default true: a command run without a pty is still a command run on the target.

directory.description: Directory is where the files are written. Required. It must exist: the proxy does not create it, because where these files live is a decision to make rather than to inherit.

enabled.description: Enabled is how a principal turns off a listener's recording; it defaults to true wherever the section is present.

file_prefix.description: FilePrefix begins each file name. Default "session".

input.description: Input records what was typed as well as what was shown. Default false, and it warns: a terminal's input stream carries what the screen never showed, which includes every password typed into a sudo or a su prompt. Recording output is watching over a shoulder; recording input is a keylogger, and the difference matters both to the people recorded and to whoever holds the files.

max_file_bytes.description: MaxFileBytes bounds one recording. Past it the session goes on unrecorded and the file says so, rather than one command that prints for an hour filling a disk. Default 33554432.

max_files.description: MaxFiles keeps this many recordings, removing the oldest this listener wrote. Default 1000. It bounds what the proxy leaves behind; anything that must be kept belongs somewhere the proxy does not prune.

SessionTickets.description: SessionTickets configures shared, rotating TLS session ticket keys.

rotate.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

secret_file.description: SecretFile is the master keyring (created when missing, 0600); deploy the same file to every node of a cluster. Rotate the master with xproxyctl rotate-secret.

Shedding.description: Shedding configures adaptive load shedding (AMR-022). The load level is the larger of the in-flight ratio (in-flight requests over max_concurrent_requests) and the latency level (how far recent upstream latency exceeds target_latency, reaching 1 at twice the target). A priority class is shed while the level is at or above its threshold, with hysteresis so that admission does not flap.

hysteresis.description: Hysteresis is subtracted from a threshold before a class is admitted again. Default 0.1.

low.description: Thresholds per class as a load level between 0 and 1. Defaults: low 0.6, normal 0.8, high 0.95. Critical is never shed.

retry_after.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

target_latency.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

SourceRate.description: SourceRate bounds accepts per second from one source network. The key is a network rather than an address on purpose: an attacker with a /64 of IPv6 has more addresses than any table could hold, so a per address bound is no bound at all, while a per address table is itself the thing that fills up.

ipv4_prefix.description: IPv4Prefix and IPv6Prefix are the network sizes the rate is counted over. Defaults 32 and 64: one IPv4 address, and the smallest IPv6 block an operator is normally given.

max_sources.description: MaxSources bounds the table of tracked networks. Default 65536.

address.description: Address is the socket path for unix (default /dev/log) or host:port.

app_name.description: AppName is the APP-NAME or tag. Default xproxy.

facility.description: Facility is kern, user, daemon, auth, authpriv, syslog, local0 to local7. Default local0.

format.description: Format is rfc5424 or rfc3164 with the JSON line as the message, or cef or leef with the record rendered in that format behind an RFC 5424 header (RFC 3164 for unix). Default rfc3164 for unix, rfc5424 otherwise.

hostname.description: Hostname overrides the HOSTNAME field. Default the OS host name.

network.description: Network is unix, udp, tcp or tcp+tls. Default unix.

queue_size.description: QueueSize bounds messages waiting for a slow or unreachable collector; beyond it messages are dropped and counted. Default 8192.

SyslogListener.description: SyslogListener is a syslog relay that reads what it forwards. A relay that forwards syslog without reading it is a pipe. The reason to read it is that almost every field is written by the sender and believed by the collector: the host name, the facility, the severity, the time. A message claiming to be auth.emerg from another machine costs nothing to send, and a message carrying a newline in its text becomes two records in any collector that frames on newlines — the second one saying whatever the sender wanted a record to say. So every message is parsed, and every message is re-emitted as RFC 5424 in one framing, whatever arrived. One dialect out is what makes the record a collector stores the record the relay decided about.

allow_facilities.description: AllowFacilities and DenySeverities filter by what the message claims to be. Empty allows everything.

allow_senders.description: AllowSenders restricts senders to these CIDRs. On UDP this is the only authentication there is.

deny_patterns.description: DenyPatterns drop a message whose text matches, as RE2. It is a filter, not a redaction: a message that matches does not arrive.

framing.description: Framing accepted on the stream side: octet_counting (RFC 6587 section 3.4.1), non_transparent (section 3.4.2, line endings) or auto. Default auto.

hostname.description: Hostname decides what the HOSTNAME field says: keep takes the sender's word, observed replaces it with the address the message arrived from, and annotate keeps it and records the address in structured data. Default annotate — the sender's name is often the useful one and is never the true one.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_message_bytes.description: MaxMessageBytes bounds one message. Default 8192. RFC 5426 requires every receiver to take 480, and most estates send more.

max_senders.description: MaxSenders bounds the rate limit table. Default 65536.

min_severity.description: MinSeverity drops anything less severe, by name: "warning" keeps emerg through warning. Empty keeps everything.

queue.description: Queue is how many parsed messages wait for the collector. Default 4096. When it is full the relay drops and counts rather than blocking every sender behind one slow collector.

rate_limit.description: RateLimit is messages per second accepted from one sender, with a burst. 0 is no limit. A log flood is a denial of service on the collector and a way to push older records out of whatever window it keeps.

redact.description: Redact replaces what matches with a fixed string, so the record still arrives without the part that should not be stored.

tls_mode.description: TLSMode is implicit (TLS from the first octet on the stream side, as RFC 5425 defines) or none. Default implicit when tls is set.

udp.description: UDP also listens on the same address for datagrams, which is what most senders still use (RFC 5426). Default true.

upstream.description: Upstream is the collector pool. Required.

upstream_framing.description: UpstreamFraming is what the relay writes: octet_counting or non_transparent. Default octet_counting, which is the only one that cannot be confused by what a message contains and the only one RFC 5425 allows over TLS.

upstream_tls.description: UpstreamTLS verifies the collector when upstream_tls_mode is not none.

upstream_tls_mode.description: UpstreamTLSMode is none or implicit. Default none.

SyslogRedaction.description: SyslogRedaction replaces what matches a pattern in a message.

pattern.description: Pattern is RE2, matched against the message text.

name.description: Name appears in the structured data the relay adds, so a reader knows something was taken out and which rule took it.

TCPListener.description: TCPListener routes raw connections to upstream pools. TLS connections are routed by the server name of the ClientHello (peeked, never terminated); other connections and unmatched names go to the default upstream when one is set and are closed otherwise.

allow_destinations.description: AllowDestinations are the CIDRs an original destination may be in, and DestinationPorts the ports; empty ports allow any.

connect_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

default.description: Default is the upstream for connections without a matching SNI (including non-TLS ones).

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_bytes_in.description: MaxBytesIn bounds what one connection relays from the client and MaxBytesOut what it relays back. Past either the connection is closed, rather than the stream being truncated: a relay that silently stopped forwarding would look to both peers like a network that had gone quiet. Both default 0, no bound.

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds open connections on this listener (in addition to the global limits). Default 10000.

original_destination.description: OriginalDestination takes the target from the socket rather than from routes or default: a transparently intercepted connection was addressed to some service and a routing rule put it on this listener, so which upstream is not a configuration question. With it, allow_destinations is required: a listener that dials whatever the firewall hands it, with nothing to say where that may be, is a relay to anywhere for anyone who can reach the port.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header to the upstream with the client address.

quic.description: QUIC also relays QUIC (UDP on the same address): the ClientHello of each flow is read from the Initial packet and routed by server name to the same upstreams. Default false.

quic_idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

transparent.description: Transparent makes the upstream connection carry the client's own source address, for an upstream that must see the client and has no PROXY protocol to read it from.

yara.description: YARA applies rules to the bytes of each connection. It does not apply to QUIC flows: those are encrypted, and a rule over ciphertext matches nothing.

TCPRoute.description: TCPRoute maps server names (exact or *.suffix) to an upstream.

TLS.description: TLS configures server side TLS for a listener.

acme.description: ACME lists host groups that get an automatically issued certificate each (one certificate per group, hosts as SANs). Requires the top-level acme section.

cipher_suites.description: CipherSuites optionally restricts TLS 1.2 suites (TLS 1.3 suites are not configurable in Go). Names as in crypto/tls, e.g. TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.

client_auth.description: ClientAuth is one of none, request, require. Default none.

client_ca_file.description: ClientCAFile is a PEM bundle used to verify client certificates.

ct.description: CT checks the signed certificate timestamps embedded in the file certificates at load.

ech.description: ECH accepts Encrypted Client Hello on this listener.

key_exchange.description: KeyExchange is the offered key agreement groups in preference order: X25519MLKEM768 (post-quantum hybrid), X25519, P-256, P-384, P-521. Empty means the default, which leads with the hybrid.

ocsp_stapling.description: OCSPStapling fetches OCSP responses for the served certificates and staples them into handshakes.

TelnetListener.description: TelnetListener is a telnet gateway: the proxy is a telnet server to the client and a telnet client to the target, reading the NVT protocol of RFC 854 in both directions. The reason it is not a tcp listener: telnet's options are commands escaped into the byte stream, so a proxy that does not parse them cannot tell a window size from the characters a person typed. Every control this listener has needs that parse -- a session recording that holds what was seen rather than what was negotiated, an option policy, and a second factor asked for before the target is dialled at all. Telnet carries everything in clear. Wrapping the listener in TLS (the tls section, as telnets does on 992) is the only thing that changes that, and validation says so when it is left off.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs.

allow_options.description: AllowOptions are the telnet options a session may negotiate, by the names in docs/CONFIG.md. Default is the set an interactive session needs and nothing else. An option this proxy has no name for is always refused: one whose effect it cannot name is one it cannot hold to a policy.

banner.description: Banner replaces what the proxy says before the target is dialled. A banner naming the equipment is a banner that saves an attacker a question.

deny_options.description: DenyOptions removes from AllowOptions, for changing one thing without restating the list.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 1000.

mfa.description: MFA asks for a login name and a one-time code before the target is dialled. Telnet has no authentication of its own for a proxy to read, so this is a prompt the proxy writes and reads itself; the target's own login happens afterwards, unchanged.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header with the client address to the target.

recording.description: Recording writes the session -- what the target showed, and optionally what was typed -- to a file.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of targets. Required.

TokenExchange.description: TokenExchange is an RFC 8693 exchange at the token endpoint. A token the client sent to the gateway is a token the gateway forwards, and everything behind the gateway then holds a credential that works at the gateway. That is the confused-deputy problem in one sentence: a backend with a bug — a log line, an error page, an outbound request to somewhere it should not go — leaks a token that reaches the front door again with all of the client's scopes on it. Exchange replaces it. The proxy presents the verified client token to the authorization server and asks for one issued for *this* backend: a different audience, usually fewer scopes, and no standing anywhere else. The backend never sees the client's token, so there is nothing there to leak that would work at the gateway. The client's identity survives — the authorization server puts the same subject in the new token, which is what makes this an exchange rather than an impersonation.

required.description: Required refuses the request when the exchange fails. Default true: forwarding the client's token after failing to replace it would quietly undo the control on exactly the requests where it went wrong.
